ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Streetlights in cities, the power supply lines of trolleybuses, etc., are often suspended using triangular structures. The figure shows a simplified model of this type of structure: the left end of a rigid rod can rotate without friction about an axis passing through point B and perpendicular to the plane of the paper; the right end, point O, is suspended from point A by a steel cable. The weights of the steel cable and the rigid rod can both be ignored. A heavy object of constant mass is suspended at point O. Now the steel cable is slowly shortened, and the suspension point A of the steel cable is slowly moved downward, so as to ensure that the rigid rod is always horizontal. Then during the above process, which of the following statements is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The pulling force exerted by the steel cable on point O becomes larger

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Streetlights in cities, the power supply lines of trolleybuses, etc., often use triangular structures for suspension. The weights of the steel cable and the rigid rod can both be neglected. A heavy object of unchanged mass is suspended at point O. Now the steel cable is slowly shortened, and the suspension point A of the steel cable is slowly moved downward, so as to ensure that the rigid rod is always horizontal. Question: during the above process of change, how does the tension exerted by the steel cable on point O change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The pulling force exerted by the steel cable on point O becomes larger
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, on the left side is a vertical wall, and point A is above point B; at point B there is a hinge point, and a horizontal rigid rod extends from point B to the right to point O; below point O is suspended a heavy object; from point A to point O there is a steel cable slanting downward, forming a triangular supporting structure. Then reason: let the angle between the steel cable AO and the horizontal rigid rod BO be θ. The system changes slowly, and can be regarded as being in static equilibrium at every instant. Taking moments about point B as the axis of rotation, the hinge reaction force at point B has zero moment about point B, and the weights of the rod and the steel cable are neglected; the weight mg of the heavy object at point O produces a clockwise moment, and the vertical component Tsinθ of the steel-cable tension T produces a counterclockwise moment. The equilibrium condition is Tsinθ·BO=mg·BO, so T=mg/sinθ. Since the rigid rod BO is always horizontal and its length is unchanged, the downward movement of point A makes the height of A relative to B decrease, and the angle θ between the steel cable and the horizontal rod becomes smaller, so sinθ becomes smaller; while mg is unchanged, therefore T=mg/sinθ becomes larger.
